🇲🇽📈 <u>Consumer confidence climbs as inflation cools</u>

Mexican consumer confidence rose to 45 points in July — its biggest monthly gain of 2026 and the highest reading since October 2025 — as INEGI credited decelerating inflation and a steadier recovery, El Economista reports. Households’ view of the current economy jumped 1.7 points and their expectations for the year ahead rose 1.8. With inflation now near 3.2%, the mood is turning.
banner: CONSUMER CONFIDENCE UP, HIGHEST SINCE OCT

🇲🇽🎓 <u>37,503 university seats — no entrance exam, no fees</u>

Mexico just opened 37,503 public university places with no admission exam and no tuition, scrapping the filter that used to brand rejected students “los rechazados.” “This is called inclusion, against exclusion,” said Sheinbaum, as Education Secretary Mario Delgado reported 74.2% of applicants placed in their first choice. Public higher education treated as a right, not a lottery.

🇲🇽💧 <u>Two firms barred for faking documents on water contracts</u>

Mexico’s Anticorruption Ministry blacklisted Limpieza Géminis and Transmareli for handing Semarnat and Conagua falsified papers to win public contracts — including ten forged professional credentials. The fines are modest — 158,369 and 814,608 pesos — but both firms are now shut out of every government contract and logged in the public registry of sanctioned suppliers.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico’s business dynasties bankroll the anti-4T opposition</u>

Twenty foundations tied to Mexico’s richest families moved 2.717 billion pesos in 2025 — the equivalent of over 424,000 elderly pensions — and Contralínea traces a slice of it straight into the opposition’s think-tank ecosystem: IMCO, México Evalúa, MCCI, Aspen México. Fundación Coppel alone gave 575 million; the Diez Morodo fortune funneled 5 million pesos into the Consejo Mexicano de Negocios, which in turn seeded IMCO and México Evalúa. As USAID cash dries up, Mexico’s oligarchy is quietly picking up the tab.

🇲🇽💵 <u>Mexicans abroad send home a record $30.7 billion</u>

Despite Trump’s deportation machine and ICE raids, remittances to Mexico hit a record 30,759 million dollars in the first half of 2026 — up 3.1% — with the average transfer climbing 5% to $405. Fewer transactions, bigger checks: the money migrants send home is worth nearly 4% of Mexico’s economy, a lifeline no border wall has managed to cut.

🇲🇽🌾 <u>Washington’s quota knife hits Mexico’s cane farmers</u>

For five years the US quietly strangled Mexico’s sugar export quota — from about 1 million tons down to 188,000, a 76% collapse — dumping the surplus back onto cañeros and crushing their prices, even as US high-fructose corn syrup flows freely south under the T-MEC. Growers call it not overproduction but “an artificial displacement caused by a trade agreement that today only protects American fructose.” Sheinbaum has now clawed the 2026-27 quota back to 576,000 tons — a 200% jump — to shore up 500,000 cane-farming families.
banner: SUGAR: US SLASHED QUOTA 76%, NOW x3 BACK

"We'll keep coming to Michoacán to advance peace and justice for its people." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 24 Sheinbaum sent Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez and Welfare Secretary Leticia Ramírez to walk communities door to door for four days in municipalities hit by rising extortion. Part of the Plan Michoacán por la Paz y la Justicia — 12 lines of action, 100+ measures, 57+ billion pesos.

🇲🇽🌎 Mexico to Washington: drop the steel and aluminum tariffs. "I'm optimistic we can reach a deal where we don't keep tariffs on aluminum and steel." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 24 Marcelo Ebrard is in the US negotiating; Sheinbaum expects clarity this week amid the USMCA review. She has answered Trump by letter on tariffs — pressing for dialogue, on terms of mutual respect and sovereignty.

🇲🇽🎨 37,503 university places. No entrance exam. No fees. "In the last two years, 245,111 new places were created in public universities." — Mario Delgado, Education Secretary, mañanera Aug 24 From tomorrow the Educación Superior 2026 platform offers 37,503 spots — 18,674 in-person, 18,629 online/hybrid — to students who didn't place at UNAM. Of 191,069 direct-access applications in the Valle de México, 93.9% got a first or second choice. Education as a right, not a lottery.
